original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Read #2973 error description and MATH.md; manually reconstruct the prefix states of 01021323 before running any large census.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no full enumeration or mathematical validation.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

actual_scope: Audit connector-covering-code Engine::enumerate gap-domain coverage, interruption/result propagation, and verify_cycles.py full-caller receipt admission, taking PR3276's explicit remaining handoff.
scope_change_reason: The original parity prune and successor capacity/representation/propagation/search layers already have focused checks. This audit closes the downstream enumeration and caller implication without repeating those results or running a complete seven-label census.
bottleneck_link: A later corrected exclusion requires complete traversal and fail-closed caller admission. This audit checks that precise implication, not the full mathematical theorem or a supplier gain.
stop_rule: Finish one source-bound traversal/caller audit with an independent gap-rank oracle and rejecting controls. Do not expand into a complete B census, new alphabet, supplier or multiplication claim.
evidence: README.md proof; RESULT.json exact counters and environment; verify.py/enumerate_harness.cpp actual-source traversal audit; check_caller.py actual caller contract; check_boundaries.py source controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Automated drafting and implementation support was used; no independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.first_step: Pin the predecessor and run its registered replay under an explicit separate resource budget, then design an independent implementation without treating timeouts as exclusions.
open_questions.blocked_by: Full replay and independent solver coverage were deliberately not included in this session.

open_questions.question: Does the cited published covering-code/classification material imply the exact walk reductions used by the successor?

open_questions.first_step: Inspect the cited literature and its exact transcribed representatives; audit the classification-to-walk correspondence.
open_questions.blocked_by: Published classification and full theorem verification are outside the traversal/caller boundary.
